title: Inconsistent shape resolution scope when using dataclasses
author: jpthalman

comments.author: patrick-kidger
comments.body:
This is intended. jaxtyping only sees the type hint you've written directly in-line, which in this case is `Vector`. It will then essentially do `isinstance(..., Vector)`, which passes. Job done. This is normal Python behaviour, `isinstance` against a class is 'shallow' and doesn't try to recursively check every sub-object contained within the class.

I think the behaviour you're after here is obtainable, though! You'd need to override `type(Vector).__instancecheck__` so that the `isinstance` will only pass if `isinstance(v.x, Vector.x) and isinstance(v.y, Vector.y)`.

Finally I'd note that you're using `chex.dataclass`. If you're here and using the Equinox ecosystem then you might like [`equinox.Module`](https://github.com/patrick-kidger/equinox), which is similar but fixes several footguns too. (Inheritance, bound methods, new stuff like abstract variables, ...)

I hope that helps!
